newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean grain output seen used up by this month.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean grain output seen used up by this month.

text.p: North Korea's grain output last year was well below half its annual needs and the impoverished state must have almost completely depleted it by this month, South Korea's state research group said on Monday.

The Korea Rural Economic Institute estimated North Korea's grain output at between 2.45 million and 2.82 million tonnes in the year to November 1996, compared with its annual requirements of between 6.06 million and 6.23 million tonnes.

"Excluding some 500,000 tonnes and one million tonnes of output already used up during 1996 and in view of the minimum food ration of 458 grammes per person per day, the 1996 output would almost completely be depleted by April," it said in a statement.
It said the Stalinst country's grain needs included non-food requirements. North Korea's annual food needs are put at 4.39 million and 4.49 million tonnes.
The institute's estimate compares with the Seoul government's projection of 3.69 million tonnes for North Korea's 1996 food harvest.
International aid groups have said famine in North Korea is just weeks away. North Korea has told United Nations aid groups that a total of 134 children have died of malnutrition.
